It was very likely that it reduced risk, because refloating a holed vessel into the channel on a falling tide with 38 passengers aboard would have put a flooding compartment into deep water.
  • The hypothesis that the tide was set down below prediction was considered and was not supported, and it was very unlikely that it was so. The Port Authority gauge read 0.91 m at 18:12 against a predicted 0.94 m. The vessel touched because it was 54 m outside a channel dredged to 3.2 m.
  • The hypothesis of a steering or propulsion failure before the vessel left the centreline was considered and was not supported, and it was very unlikely that it was so. Engine speeds, steering gear hydraulic pressure and rudder response were normal throughout, the heading change was applied and held, and the steering system tested serviceable after the occurrence.
  • It was virtually certain that 14 unshielded LED floodlights at the new boat ramp, each presenting about 4,800 candela toward the channel, lay behind the No. 4 beacon within 4 degrees of the same bearing from 0.5 nm north of it. Whether they delayed the sighting in the seconds after the beacon cleared the islet was as likely as not, and this was not settled. The master described looking "into a wall of light", and the outgoing master independently called the beacon "washed out altogether from up the top". Against that, the canopy screened the beacon over most of the search, the heading change began before the search, no measurement was made on the night, nothing established a detection threshold for a 0.4 second flash against that background, and the master said twice that it could not be told whether the lights were why the beacon was not seen. A measurement of detection of the beacon against the lighting under the conditions of the night would be needed to settle it.
  • It was as likely as not that the master was fatigued during the channel transit, and this was not settled. The master was on day nine of a twelve-day tour, had 6 hours 15 minutes of sleep and said "I was tired." Easing back rather than stopping while nearly 40 m west of the centreline is a misjudgement fatigue is expected to produce. Against that, the master said they were not fighting to stay awake and were not slow, the centreline was held to within 3 m for the first two minutes in the channel, the response to the shallow alarm took 4 seconds, and the radio work after the grounding was complete at the first attempt. No detailed fatigue assessment was made, so the evidence either way could not be weighed further.

Safety action and recommendations

This section describes the action already taken in response to the occurrence and the recommendations made where a safety issue remained open. Two safety issues have action recorded against them, and two have recommendations.

Safety action taken

Clearing of the beacon's sightline

The Harbour Master, Kanooka Heads, funded work order WO-176 from the 2026 waterways contingency. The Merrandi Islet canopy was trimmed to 2 m on 24 July 2026, which restored the No. 4 beacon's sightline over the northern approach. A three-yearly trimming cycle has been programmed, and the sightline was re-measured from the inbound track on completion. The action is recorded as closed.

This action answers in full the safety issue that clearing of the beacon's sightline was deferred, unfunded, for three works rounds. The canopy had measured 5.8 m against a lantern height of 4.2 m, and the trimming and the programmed cycle correspond to the work recommended in WO-118 in September 2023. The action trimmed the vegetation and programmed the cycle. It did not change the scope in schedule 2.4 of the services agreement that had kept the work in the general waterways vote, and that matter is the subject of the first recommendation below.

Change to the No. 4 beacon's range

The Aids to Navigation Officer, Kanooka Shire Council, issued local notice to waterway users LNM-2026-14 on 22 July 2026. It gave the No. 4 beacon's solar conversion and its 3 M nominal range, and the Port Authority's aids to navigation register was made available to every commercial operator using the channel. Tarrakin Ferries has reissued the Merrandi Channel passage plan appendix as issue 3 with the corrected range. This action is recorded as in progress.

The action answers in part the safety issue that the beacon's range was halved by solar conversion with no notice to channel users. The notice and the release of the register address the absence of any local notice and the fact that the register had never been provided to Tarrakin Ferries. The reissued appendix corrects the 6 M range that the operator's plan had carried. The range check of 18 July 2026 gave a luminous range of 2.6 nm, and the chart correction lodged with the hydrographic service on 4 February 2026 was still pending on 7 July 2026. The action does not provide for notice to channel users of any later change to a beacon's range, character or position, because section 4.2 of the Waterways Aids to Navigation Code WAN-2 does not apply to the Merrandi Channel and the services agreement requires no notification of any change to an aid.

Safety issues with no action recorded

[NOT ESTABLISHED: any recommendation or safety action on the OPS-9 defect procedure, the RRA-07 and change-control process, the echo sounder alarm setting, the WAN-2 notice and availability duty, the roster, or the foreshore lighting assessment]

[NOT ESTABLISHED: any safety action or recommendation on the forward saloon lifejacket locker, including the operator's and the regulator's answers on the other two vessels]

[NOT ESTABLISHED: the Port Authority's or Council's response on a lighting assessment of the channel]

Safety recommendations

The Investigator in charge made the following two recommendations on 27 July 2026. Both are open and a response is due by 30 September 2026.

Aids to navigation services agreement: vegetation scope

The issue is that the 50 m vegetation scope at schedule 2.4 of the aids to navigation services agreement put a screening canopy 240 m from the beacon into the general waterways vote. There it competed with boat ramps and was deferred for three works rounds while the beacon it screened continued to be charted as lit.

It is recommended that the Kanooka Shire Council and the Kanooka Heads Port Authority replace the 50 m vegetation scope at schedule 2.4 of the aids to navigation services agreement with a sightline test, so that work needed to keep an aid visible from the water it serves is funded as an aid to navigation whatever its distance from the structure.

Night passage plan for the Merrandi Channel

The issue is that Tarrakin Ferries had no night passage plan for the Merrandi Channel and no hold point for loss of the primary means of position fixing. Both masters interviewed said independently that stopping was the right answer and that nothing anywhere asked for it.

It is recommended that Tarrakin Ferries write a night passage plan for the Merrandi Channel before any further darkness transit, and that the plan name a hold point under which the loss of the primary means of position fixing inside the channel requires the way to be taken off the vessel until the position is re-established by another means.
